en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga,
Chapter on Offenses Entailing Expiation (Pācittiyakaṇḍa)
The Chapter on Drinking Liquor, 59.
The Training Rule on Transferring Possessions.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the Venerable Upananda the Sakyan had personally assigned a robe to a bhikkhu who was his brother’s student, and he used it without having formally relinquished it.
Then that bhikkhu informed the bhikkhus of this matter, saying:
"Friends, this Venerable Upananda the Sakyan has personally assigned a robe to me and is using it without having formally relinquished it."
Those monks who were few in desires... they complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
“How can the Venerable Upananda the Sakyaputta, having himself assigned a robe to a monk, use it without having it formally relinquished? ... [Upāli asked:
“Is it true, Upananda, that you, having yourself assigned a robe to a monk, used it without having it formally relinquished?”
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him:
“… How can you, foolish man, having personally assigned a robe to a monk, use it without having formally relinquished the assignment?”
“Worthless man, this does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:

‘If any monk, having himself assigned a robe to a monk, a nun, a trainee nun, a novice monk, or a novice nun, should use it without it being relinquished, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).’”
"But whoever" means whoever such as this...
"monk" means... [as before].
...pe... this is the "bhikkhu" intended in this context.
"Of a bhikkhu" means of another bhikkhu.
A bhikkhunī is one who has received full ordination in both Saṅghas.
A sikkhamānā is one who...
One who has trained in the training regarding the six rules for two years [is a novice].
A novice (sāmaṇera) is one who observes ten precepts.
A *sāmaṇerī* is one who observes the ten precepts.
*Sāmā* means...
Having made the assignment oneself.
"Robe" means any one of the six kinds of robes that is suitable for assignment and is of the lowest quality.
"Designation" means two kinds of designation: face-to-face designation and behind-the-back designation.
Face-to-face designation means...
“I assign this robe to you, or to [name].
What is called “assignment in the absence” is:
“I give this robe to you for the purpose of assignment.”
He should be asked: "Who are your friends or acquaintances?
[If he replies: "So-and-so and so-and-so," he should be told: "I give these to them; use what belongs to them, or dispose of it, or do with it as you see fit."
"Without having had it formally relinquished" means:
he either uses what has not been given back to him, or he uses it without being confident that it will be returned; there is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*).
If it has not been formally relinquished and he perceives it as such, yet he uses it, there is an offense of expiation.
If one consumes [food] while it has not been formally relinquished, yet one is in doubt about it, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If one consumes [food] while it has not been formally relinquished and one perceives it as such, there is an offense of expiation.
If one resolves upon it or gives it away, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If there is relinquishment, but one perceives it as not relinquished, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If there is relinquishment, but one is uncertain about it, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If there is relinquishment, and one perceives it as relinquished, there is no offense.
There is no offense if he gives it himself,
or if one uses it while placing trust in him.
"In the case of one who is insane,
and in the case of the first offender.
The ninth training rule on assigning [an item] is finished.
